steps.what: Select current programs and schedules and verify source versions and media recipients
Assemble programme titles, descriptions and schedules into the media information format
Review programme information for accuracy and send the accepted version to local media outlets

tasks.design: Configure an export template from {OTHER}, the broadcast scheduling system, into {DOCS}. The director verifies exact programme descriptions, times and recipients before sending the information through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Copying schedule fields into outlet formats repeated work and introduced transcription errors.
tasks.enabler_now: Native exports and document templates can assemble explicit fields from a checked version.
tasks.still_hard: Schedule changes, sensitive descriptions and publication timing still need editorial attention.
tasks.human_edge: The director knows which programme information is accurate and appropriate to release now.
tasks.altitude: Less information assembly; external release responsibility remains with the director.

reach.task: Verify published programme details against primary material

evidence.claim: A configured schedule export can populate a fixed media information template without interpreting programme content; the proposed saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is reviewing and providing programme information to media outlets, excluding scheduling decisions, promotional concept development and outlets' publication work. Reuse source data without counting its creation again.

Schedulers produce accepted identifiers, titles, channel, start, duration and schedule version; programme editors produce description text and version through existing work. Director verifies and captures selected versions, reporting period, timezone, approved description text, recipient addresses and release timing in s1's 30 hours.

s2 consumes only the checked manifest and exact source fields. Missing metadata, changed schedules or incompatible outlet formats return to manual assembly and checking in s3; no model rewrites descriptions or infers a release permission.
Test native export configuration first. s3's 45 hours include accuracy, version and recipient checks, exceptions and human sending; no automatic external distribution is proposed.
unknowns: Whether native exports support the required outlet format
How often schedules change between preparation and release
research_questions: Does the exported draft preserve exact descriptions, timezone and latest accepted schedule without extra checking effort?

already_counted.description: Capture source versions and recipients, verify information and handle manual exceptions before sending

incremental.description: Maintain export templates and outlet field mappings

approvals.approved_version: Exact outgoing information attachment or body, schedule and description versions, recipient list and release time; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75, gross=25; minus 7 focal upkeep gives central net=18. Range assumes only some outlet formats are reusable and late changes require manual rebuilding; release checking and sending keep full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set budgets and monitor broadcasting spend

steps.what: Develop programming and broadcasting budgets and specify expenditure categories and limits
Compile expenditures and compare category totals with budgetary limits
Investigate expenditure variances and decide programming budget or spending responses

tasks.design: Configure budget-versus-expenditure views in {ERP} using the director's explicit budget categories and limits from {SPREADSHEET}. Keep allocation choices, investigation and responses human; the view neither blocks spending nor changes budgets automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated compilation of spend obscured the time needed to investigate departures from plans.
tasks.enabler_now: Native budget views can compare recorded amounts with versioned limits using fixed grouping rules.
tasks.still_hard: A variance may reflect timing, a valid editorial change or an actual budget problem.
tasks.human_edge: The director weighs financial consequences against programming needs and negotiates an appropriate response.
tasks.altitude: Less mechanical spend compilation; budget judgement and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Committed costs, actual costs and production uncertainty

evidence.claim: Native financial reporting can sum expenditures and compare them with explicit budget categories and limits; the task saving is an unmeasured model scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is programming budget development and expenditure monitoring, excluding invoice entry, payment approval and production-specific management views owned by other tasks. Each compilation action has one owner.

Finance staff produce expenditure identifier, programme or cost centre, period, amount, currency, committed or actual status and ledger version through normal accounting after costs arise and before each s2 refresh. Extra field upkeep is counted below.

Director captures budget version, category mapping, included cost centres, period, currency, committed versus actual treatment, category limits and escalation thresholds in s1's 30 hours. Budget choice and capture are retained human effort, not free input preparation.

Unmatched categories, mixed currencies or unclear commitment status remain explicit exceptions and are investigated manually in s3's 50 hours. No machine flag establishes that an expense is justified or that an overspend is authorized.
Try native financial reports first. Existing finance approval requirements remain in place; s3 accepts the director's budget proposals and response instructions, not payments.
unknowns: Whether financial records distinguish commitments from actuals consistently
Which budget changes the director can approve independently
research_questions: Does a native view reproduce past category totals without double-counting committed and actual costs?

already_counted.description: Capture budget definitions, investigate variances and accept responses

incremental.description: Maintain mappings and retest reporting definitions

approvals.approved_version: Exact budget version, expenditure snapshot, variance interpretation and director-authorized response instructions; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80, gross=20; minus 7 focal upkeep gives central net=13. Range assumes incomplete categories and manual cost interpretation. Three other-role upkeep hours are outside the focal denominator; no finance processing time is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Cue announcers, actors, performers and guests at the appropriate performance moment

tasks.design: Keep participant cueing human, using the existing running order in {DOCS} when required. The director observes readiness and live context before giving each cue.
tasks.previous_blocker: The correct cue depends on what is happening now and whether the participant is ready.
tasks.enabler_now: Current running orders and communication arrangements already support cueing.
tasks.still_hard: Late changes, hesitation and performance interruptions need immediate human judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The director reads readiness and adjusts the cue to the actual performance.
tasks.altitude: Cueing time and authority remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Live production timing and communication conventions

evidence.claim: Live participant cueing requires contextual human judgement; no labour saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary is the human cue itself, excluding creating the running order, technical transmission automation and participant preparation.

Production coordinators produce running orders through normal work; participants demonstrate readiness in the live interaction. Director observes and checks readiness within the retained 100 hours, without a free structured ready flag.
Keep current native records and cueing arrangements. No new capture, system or process means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Which cues occur live and which during recording
How cue authority is divided across production staff
research_questions: Are cueing responsibility and communication conventions clear to each participant?

already_counted.description: Observe readiness and give live participant cues

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Live cueing retains all human effort; no timer runtime is treated as saved labour.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Act as a liaison to understand performer and guest preparation needs and information
Provide preparation information to talent and communicate relevant guest and staff information to directors

tasks.design: Keep talent liaison human, using {EMAIL} and existing appearance briefs in {DOCS}. The director clarifies needs before communicating the relevant information to each party and confirming shared understanding.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information may be incomplete, sensitive or understood differently by guests and production staff.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing brief records and communication tools already support the exchange.
tasks.still_hard: Judging relevance, tone and what can appropriately be shared requires interpersonal context.
tasks.human_edge: The liaison builds trust and notices confusion before an appearance.
tasks.altitude: Preparation liaison and communication responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare performers and guests for an appearance
reach.learn: Expectation setting and sensitive information handling

evidence.claim: Talent liaison combines contextual communication and clarification; no separate clerical baseline or labour saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is the information exchange between talent and directors, excluding booking, casting, contracts, transport and live cueing. Do not add the same liaison effort twice in team roll-ups.

Guests, performers and production staff produce their questions and requirements during normal participation. Director elicits, checks and records relevant information in s1 and communicates it in s2, with all time retained; no free structured preparation record is assumed.
Existing sharing permissions and appearance arrangements remain in place. Keep native briefs and communication; no new tool or process means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Which preparation questions recur and which require private discussion
Who may receive sensitive guest information
research_questions: Do guests and directors leave preparation exchanges with the same understanding of the appearance?

already_counted.description: Clarify preparation needs and communicate relevant information to both parties

incremental.description: No new system or process upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Clarification and liaison retain full time; routine wording is not assumed to replace the information exchange.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The director can reduce repeated programme-information assembly and budget arithmetic while retaining external release, live cueing and personal liaison.
reach: Learn preparation practices from talent directors
skills_to_grow: Verify source versions before sending programme information
Communicate clear and appropriate appearance expectations
role.ambitious_version: Provide accurate programme information and financial oversight while keeping live and interpersonal decisions with accountable people.
